encounters.cc: Comes to the hematology clinic for follow-up after completing her first cycle of chemotherapy for a recently diagnosed lymphoid malignancy

lines: Comes to the hematology clinic for follow-up after completing her first cycle of chemotherapy for a recently diagnosed lymphoid malignancy

The patient returns for follow-up after her first chemotherapy cycle with history of hepatitis C, cryoglobulinemia, porphyria cutanea tarda, and malabsorption complicated by vitamin E deficiency and ataxia.
Six months ago, she began experiencing fatigue, drenching night sweats, and an unintentional 7-kg (15-lb) weight loss.
She also noted swelling in her neck and underarms that gradually increased in size.
After the first infusion of the monoclonal antibody, she experienced transient fever, chills, and mild hypotension, which resolved with supportive care.

There is no family history of cancer.
She does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs.
On physical examination at diagnosis, she had multiple firm, nontender cervical and axillary lymph nodes.
Hepatosplenomegaly was present without abdominal tenderness.
Laboratory studies revealed mild normocytic anemia and an elevated lactate dehydrogenase level.
Peripheral blood smear showed no abnormal cells.
CT scans demonstrated diffuse lymphadenopathy above and below the diaphragm.
An excisional biopsy of a cervical lymph node revealed sheets of atypical lymphoid cells with irregular nuclear contours and scant cytoplasm.
Immunohistochemistry was positive for CD19 and CD20, but negative for CD3 and CD15.
She was counseled that these infusion reactions are common and usually diminish with subsequent doses.
